title: VMware ESXi
subtitle: A bare-metal hypervisor that partitions hardware into isolated virtual machines.

tiles.label: ESXi kernel
tiles.says: ESXi runs directly on hardware and schedules virtual CPUs.
tiles.detail: A thin type-1 hypervisor delivers near-native performance and strong isolation.

tiles.label: Datastores
tiles.says: Datastores hold virtual disks on VMFS or NFS.
tiles.detail: Thin provisioning and snapshots improve utilisation and allow quick rollback.

tiles.label: Resource control
tiles.says: Reservations, shares and limits govern CPU and memory.
tiles.detail: Predictable capacity keeps critical machines responsive.

tiles.label: vSwitches
tiles.says: vSwitches connect VMs to uplinks or to each other.
tiles.detail: A switch with no uplink creates a private network isolated from the physical LAN.

tiles.label: Port groups & VLANs
tiles.says: Port groups apply VLAN and security policy.
tiles.detail: Segmentation separates traffic types on shared hardware.

tiles.label: Gateway VM
tiles.says: A dual-NIC VM routes between public and private switches.
tiles.detail: It acts as router and firewall, publishing only what is intended.

tiles.label: Directory services
tiles.says: A domain controller supplies AD, DNS and DHCP.
tiles.detail: Central identity and naming make a private network manageable.

tiles.label: Session brokering
tiles.says: A broker routes users to available session hosts.
tiles.detail: Remote desktops scale by adding hosts.

tiles.label: File services
tiles.says: A file server holds shares and profiles.
tiles.detail: Group-based permissions and backups protect user data.

declarations: A vSwitch with no uplink is private.
One gateway VM, one controlled door.
